_comment: Design-variation tables read by scripts/roll.py. Each axis maps value-id -> short description; ids are what a game's `## Design DNA` block records (`- axis: id`). `pick` = how many distinct values one combo draws (default 1). `structure` ids MUST match story-structures/<id>.md. `high_impact` axes are the ones --avoid-recent steers away from when existing games already used them. `incompatible` lists value pairs (`axis=id`) that never appear together in one combo.

values.conspiracy-mystery: pull one thread, uncover a hidden web; a dated deadline closes in
values.heist: assemble a crew, plan the job, watch the plan break, improvise
values.siege-survival: hold one place while resources run out; hard allocations
values.political-intrigue: factions trade favors and secrets toward a scheduled decision
values.road-journey: a chain of waystations between here and there changes the traveler
values.time-loop: one stretch of time repeats; only the protagonist remembers
values.tournament-ascent: an underdog climbs a bracket of admirable rivals
values.doomed-cause: a band commits to a cause that cannot fully win; meaning over outcome
values.seasons-of-a-community: slice of life through a year of seasons, projects and festivals
values.expedition-into-unknown: a team pushes into an unmapped place and pays for every step
values.revenge: work through a list of those responsible; each name costs a piece of the self

values.single-nemesis: one person with a face, a reason, and a plan of their own
values.institution: an order, company, church or state that grinds on without malice
values.rival-peer: an equal who wants the same thing and is admirable about it
values.nature: weather, terrain, the cold, the sea, a sickness: forces without intent
values.the-party-itself: the protagonist's own side fractures: trust, loyalty, ambition
values.the-protagonists-past: an old deed, debt or identity that keeps catching up
values.faction-web: several sides, none purely villainous, each with a fair grievance
values.a-beloved-opponent: someone the protagonist loves stands on the other side
values.the-unknown: a presence or rule no one understands yet; it has patterns and moods
values.public-opinion: rumor, reputation and the crowd's mood decide what is possible
values.time-and-decay: things are ending on their own; the fight is over what remains
values.no-villain: only circumstance and the characters' own wants pull against each other

values.triumph-at-a-cost: the goal is won, and something real is paid for it
values.bittersweet: a fair outcome with an ache: someone or something is not coming back
values.pyrrhic: the victory destroys much of what it was meant to protect
values.tragic-with-meaning: it falls, but the fall says something and is remembered
values.open-question: the last scene leaves one deliberate question for the player to hold
values.transformation: the protagonist ends as someone, or something, new
values.reconciliation: estranged people come back together; the wound is shared
values.escape: leave it all behind for a different life
values.new-order: the protagonist founds, inherits or reshapes the institution
values.quiet-continuity: life goes on, richer; no grand finale, a full circle
values.sacrifice: someone chooses to give themselves so others continue
values.branching-by-allegiance: who the player sided with decides which of several endings lands

values.newcomer: an outsider arriving with no standing and fresh eyes
values.disgraced-veteran: once great at something, now blamed for a failure
values.reluctant-heir: inherits a role, a debt or a title they never wanted
values.ordinary-worker: a tradesperson with a job to keep and a skill that matters
values.fugitive: hunted for something done, or wrongly blamed for it
values.caretaker: responsible for others who depend on them
values.impostor: pretending to be someone they are not, and good at it
values.last-survivor: the only one left of a group, place or tradition
values.apprentice: learning a craft under someone with secrets
values.returning-home: coming back after years away to a place that changed
values.ruler-out-of-depth: holds authority without the experience to use it
values.hired-specialist: a professional contracted for one job that becomes more

values.grim-and-grounded: consequences are heavy; violence and loss are real
values.warm-and-cozy: low stakes, kind people, small comforts
values.wry-comedic: absurdity and wit, with sincerity underneath
values.elegiac: melancholy and beauty; things are passing
values.pulpy-adventure: fast, bold, colorful; set pieces and narrow escapes
values.tense-paranoid: trust is scarce; everyone might be lying
values.romantic: longing, chemistry and grand gestures lead the story
values.eerie: quiet wrongness, uncanny details, dread over gore
values.hopeful-heroic: courage matters and good deeds ripple outward
values.satirical: the world's systems are shown up through exaggeration
values.contemplative: slow, observant, philosophical; small moments carry weight
values.operatic: big emotions, grand betrayals, declarations under storms

values.high-fantasy: D&D-style sword-and-sorcery: adventuring parties, dungeons, dragons, guilds
values.low-fantasy: muddy, local, rare and costly magic; politics and weather matter more
values.near-future-city: a dense city a few decades ahead: tech, debt, surveillance, neon
values.far-future-space: ships, stations and colonies light-years apart
values.post-collapse: the old world ended; scavenging, rebuilding, new customs
values.invented-early-modern: an invented age of sail, printing presses, guilds and empires
values.present-day: the world as it is now, with one hidden layer or none
values.mythic-bronze-age: gods walk close; heroes, oracles and city-states
values.gaslamp-industrial: smoke, steam, factories, spiritualism and labor unrest
values.drowned-world: an ocean planet or flooded land; boats, reefs, sunken cities
values.desert-caravans: oases, trade routes, sandstorms and wandering markets
values.sky-islands: floating islands linked by airships, bridges and winds
values.martial-arts-world: sects, masters, codes of honor and rival schools
values.small-town-uncanny: a quiet town where something is slightly wrong
values.afterlife-or-dream: a realm of the dead, of dreams, or between

values.gap: a public mask hiding a very different inner self
values.debt: owes something (money, a life, a favor) and it shapes every choice
values.vow: bound by a promise that is getting harder to keep
values.faith: believes in something that is being tested
values.rivalry: defined against someone they must equal or surpass
values.mentorship: teaching or being taught; the lesson goes both ways
values.guilt: carries a wrong they did and tries to balance it
values.ambition: wants to rise and is willing to pay for it
values.duty: bound to a role or people that outranks their own wishes
values.grief: mourning someone, and the mourning steers them
values.curiosity: must know, even when knowing costs
values.belonging: wants a place and people to call home
values.freedom: wants out of a cage: a role, a contract, a destiny
values.protection: will keep someone safe at any price

values.romance: a love story at the center (activate the romance module)
values.found-family: strangers who become each other's home
values.rivalry: two equals who sharpen and provoke each other
values.mentor-student: an older hand and a learner, both adults, each changing the other
values.siblings: adult siblings bound by history and old quarrels
values.comrades-in-arms: people who have fought side by side and owe each other
values.employer-employee: a boss and a worker whose roles bend under pressure
values.old-friends-apart: friends who drifted and are thrown back together
values.partners: professional partners: detectives, traders, a two-person crew
values.parent-and-adult-child: a parent and their grown child, rebuilding or breaking
values.protector-and-charge: one adult sworn or hired to keep another adult safe

values.intimate: one house, one ship, one room's worth of people
values.personal-circle: a family, a crew, a handful of lives
values.neighborhood: a street, a village, a market quarter
values.regional: a province, a coastline, a valley of towns
values.world: the fate of the whole world or civilization
values.cosmic: gods, stars, the nature of reality itself

values.none: play it straight; no extra constraint
values.cannot-lie: the protagonist cannot speak a falsehood
values.unreliable-ally: one trusted companion is not who they claim, from the very first scene
values.begins-at-the-end: open with the final scene, then play how it came to that
values.power-has-a-price: every use of the central power or tech costs something visible
values.opponent-is-right: the opposition is right about one important thing
values.famous-for-a-lie: the protagonist is celebrated for something they did not do
values.the-map-is-wrong: a basic fact everyone believes about the world is false
values.shrinking-world: the playable world gets smaller as the story goes on
values.one-shared-body: two minds share one body, or one mind is split between two
values.letters-home: each phase ends with a letter the protagonist writes to someone absent
values.no-violence-solves-it: the central problem cannot be fixed by force
values.a-companion-creature: an animal or creature companion is central to the story
